project.name: unihack8
project.description: Hackathon mobile app for Timișoara (Connected Communities): Spring Boot API + Supabase + Expo app with events and QR reliability points, places map, live STPT transit, routing and an AI guide.

nodes.name: StptClient.java
nodes.summary: Interface for the STPT (Timisoara public transport) live-site client, declaring fetch operations for stops, routes, vehicles, arrivals and alerts.

nodes.name: StptClient
nodes.summary: Client contract for reading raw STPT stops, routes, live vehicles, stop arrivals and service alerts.

nodes.name: StptClientImpl.java
nodes.summary: Spring component that calls the undocumented STPT live-site JSON endpoints via RestClient and leniently parses them into raw Stpt* records.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) JsonNode tree parsing with null-tolerant helpers instead of strict data binding.

nodes.name: StptClientImpl
nodes.summary: RestClient-backed STPT client that parses stops index, route manifest, vehicles, arrivals and alerts JSON with lenient field handling.

nodes.name: fetchStops
nodes.summary: Fetches /gtfs-data/stops-index.json and converts the stop-id-keyed object into StptStop records.

nodes.name: fetchRoutes
nodes.summary: Fetches the route manifest and converts the line-name-keyed routes object into StptRoute records.

nodes.name: fetchVehicles
nodes.summary: Queries /gtfs-vehicles.php for a route, failing on unsuccessful answers, and maps live vehicles into StptVehicle records.

nodes.name: fetchArrivals

nodes.name: StptProperties.java
nodes.summary: Type-safe configuration properties (prefix "stpt") for the STPT base URL, HTTP timeouts, user agent and per-data-type cache TTLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record with @ConfigurationProperties and @DefaultValue gives immutable configuration with built-in defaults, including a nested Ttl record.

nodes.name: StptProperties
nodes.summary: Immutable record holding STPT connection settings and nested cache TTL durations (vehicles 10s, arrivals 20s, alerts 5m, static 24h).

nodes.name: ArrivalDto.java

nodes.name: VehicleDto.java
nodes.summary: API DTO record for one live transit vehicle shown on the map, including position, bearing, speed and accessibility.

nodes.name: StptArrival

nodes.languageNotes: Combines classic switch statements with Java switch expressions and uses java.time ZonedDateTime with a +/-12h window to resolve arrival times around midnight.

nodes.name: arrivalInstant

nodes.name: parseMinutes

nodes.name: StaleCache.java
nodes.summary: Generic thread-safe TTL cache with stale-on-failure fallback used to front unreliable upstream sources like the STPT transit feed; returns 503 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when nothing is cached.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a nested record Result<V> and per-key Slot objects as monitors so only one thread fetches a key at a time.

nodes.name: StaleCache
nodes.summary: Generic per-key cache holding values for a TTL, serving the last known value marked stale when the source fails.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns a fresh cached value or reloads it from the supplier under a per-key lock, falling back to a stale value or throwing SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

nodes.name: ErrorResponse.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record defining the single standard error JSON shape (status, code, message, field errors, timestamp, path) returned by every API endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record gives a compact immutable DTO with auto-generated accessors, equals and hashCode.

nodes.name: ErrorResponse
nodes.summary: Record holding HTTP status, machine-readable error code, message, optional per-field validation errors, UTC timestamp and request path.

nodes.name: ErrorResponseFactory.java
nodes.summary: Spring component that builds ErrorResponse objects from an ErrorCode so the controller advice and security handlers produce identical error bodies.

nodes.name: ErrorResponseFactory
nodes.summary: Clock-injected factory creating ErrorResponse instances, falling back to the ErrorCode default message and omitting empty field maps.

nodes.name: create

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler.java

nodes.languageNotes: Uses Spring @ExceptionHandler methods keyed by exception type; a catch-all Exception handler logs and hides internals.

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler
nodes.summary: Controller advice with one handler per exception type, each delegating to a shared respond helper that sets the ErrorCode HTTP status.

nodes.name: handleBodyValidation
nodes.summary: Collects field and global binding errors from a failed @Valid request body into a VALIDATION_FAILED response.

nodes.summary: Maps @RequestParam/@PathVariable constraint failures into per-parameter VALIDATION_FAILED field errors.

nodes.name: handleConstraintViolation

nodes.name: 20261113000001_profiles.sql

tour.title: Project Vision and Plan
tour.description: The README is only a title, so the real starting point is AGENTS.md, which states the Connected Communities problem, the team rules (tests for every change, keep DOCS.md and the knowledge graph current) and the core idea: a Timișoara map with places, live STPT transit, directions, an AI guide and community events with reliability points. PLAN.md turns that vision into numbered tasks split across backend, data/AI services and mobile tracks, so you can see what exists now and what comes next.

tour.title: Docs Hub and API Contract
tour.description: DOCS.md is the living map of the system: architecture, backend configuration, run instructions and the shared foundation you will meet later. docs/API.md defines how the mobile app talks to the backend (conventions, paged and error answer shapes, shared objects and endpoints, including the /transit routes), and infra/otp/README.md describes the planned OpenTripPlanner server that will compute walking and public transport directions. Reading the contract first makes the Java code later in the tour easy to follow.

tour.title: Users and Profiles Schema
tour.description: The data model starts in Supabase Postgres. Migration 1 enables pg_trgm and creates public.profiles, one row per Supabase auth user with a case-insensitive unique username, filled automatically by the on_auth_user_created trigger. Profiles are the most referenced table, because events, participation and reliability all point back to a user.
tour.languageLesson: A Postgres trigger on auth.users lets the database create the app-side profile row the moment someone signs up, so the backend never has to remember to do it.

tour.title: Events on the Map
tour.description: Building on profiles, migration 2 creates public.events for both user-created (USER) and imported (EXTERNAL) events. Check constraints enforce source rules, valid coordinates and prices at the database level, so bad data cannot reach the map no matter which client writes it.

tour.title: Participation and Reliability
tour.description: This migration models the project's signature feature. event_participants joins users to events with a status lifecycle (JOINED, ATTENDED, NO_SHOW, CANCELLED) and the QR token used for check-in, while reliability_log records every signed point change as an audit trail. Together they make reliability points explainable rather than a single opaque counter.
tour.languageLesson: An append-only log table like reliability_log is a common SQL pattern: each change is stored as a row and totals are derived from it, so history is never lost.

tour.title: Places and Schema Checks
tour.description: Migration 4 adds public.places for restaurants, cafes and other points of interest imported from OpenStreetMap, kept unique by osm_id so re-imports update rows instead of duplicating them. schema_checks.sql is a self-rolling-back PL/pgSQL block that verifies the rules from the last four steps without leaving data behind, and .mcp.json registers the hosted Supabase MCP server that AI tooling uses to inspect and migrate this database.

tour.title: Spring Boot Entry and Settings
tour.description: BackendApplication bootstraps the Spring Boot API, and its smoke test checks that the context loads. SupabaseProperties binds the Supabase URL and legacy HS256 JWT secret and derives the token issuer, TimeConfig exposes a shared UTC Clock so time logic can be tested, and application.properties tells Hibernate to only validate against the Supabase migrations and also holds the stpt.* transit settings used later.
tour.languageLesson: Java records annotated with @ConfigurationProperties give immutable, validated config objects, and injecting a Clock bean instead of calling Instant.now() lets tests freeze time.

tour.title: Security and the Current User
tour.description: SecurityConfig makes the backend a stateless JWT resource server: Supabase access tokens are validated with the secret and issuer from the previous step, public GET routes stay open, and everything else requires a token. CurrentUser reads the token's sub claim to give services the caller's UUID, and the JSON entry point and access-denied handler make 401 and 403 answers use the same error format as the rest of the API.
tour.languageLesson: In modern Spring Security you declare a SecurityFilterChain bean; configuring oauth2ResourceServer with a JWT decoder means every request is authenticated before any controller runs.

tour.title: One Error Format Everywhere
tour.description: ErrorCode is the most depended-on file in the backend: an enum listing every API error, from validation and auth to QR check-in, rate limiting and SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for upstream outages. Code throws ApiException with a code, GlobalExceptionHandler catches it, and ErrorResponseFactory builds the ErrorResponse record, the single error JSON shape promised in docs/API.md and shared with the security handlers from Step 8.
tour.languageLesson: @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler methods centralises error handling, so controllers just throw and never build error bodies themselves.

tour.title: Paging and Geo Query Helpers
tour.description: PageParams and PageResponse enforce the API paging rules and give every list endpoint the same shape. The common/geo package adds GeoPoint, which parses near=lat,lon and computes haversine distances in meters, and BoundingBox, which parses bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat and tests containment. All of them reject bad input by throwing the ApiException from Step 9, so query validation looks identical across features.
tour.languageLesson: Java records can validate their fields in a compact constructor and expose static parse factories, giving small immutable value types that are always valid once created.

tour.title: Foundation Tests with Real JWTs
tour.description: The foundation runs its tests on in-memory H2 in PostgreSQL mode with a fake Supabase secret. JwtTestTokens signs HS256 tokens shaped like real Supabase access tokens, TestProbeController (test-only) exposes probe endpoints so SecurityConfigTest and GlobalExceptionHandlerTest can check public and protected routes and the exact error JSON with MockMvc, and GeoParsingTest covers the near= and bbox= parsing from Step 10.

tour.title: StaleCache for Flaky Sources
tour.description: StaleCache is a generic, thread-safe TTL cache built to front unreliable upstreams like the STPT live feed. Fresh entries are served directly, expired ones are reloaded, and if a reload fails the last known value is returned and flagged stale; only when nothing was ever cached does it throw the 503 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE error from Step 9. StaleCacheTest drives expiry deterministically with MutableClock, a test Clock you advance by hand, building on the injected Clock from Step 7.
tour.languageLesson: Passing a loader function (a Supplier) into the cache keeps caching policy separate from fetching logic, and keying entries per data kind keeps them isolated.

tour.title: Calling live.stpt.ro
tour.description: The transit feature starts at the edge of the system. StptProperties binds the stpt.* settings (base URL, timeouts, user agent, per-data-type cache TTLs), StptClientConfig builds the RestClient with those timeouts and a custom User-Agent, and the StptClient interface with its StptClientImpl calls the undocumented STPT live-site JSON endpoints and leniently parses them into raw Stpt* records such as StptStop.
tour.languageLesson: Spring's RestClient is the modern synchronous HTTP client; configuring it once as a bean with timeouts means every call inherits safe defaults instead of hanging on a slow upstream.

tour.title: Raw STPT Data to API DTOs
tour.description: The project keeps two DTO families: raw stpt records mirroring the upstream format (like StptArrival with its HH:mm|minutes strings) and clean API records like ArrivalDto and VehicleDto that match docs/API.md. TransitMapperImpl bridges them by hand: it splits route ends, classifies vehicle types and converts local Timișoara arrival times into UTC instants, even across midnight.
tour.languageLesson: java.time separates LocalTime (wall clock) from Instant (absolute time); combining a LocalTime with a ZoneId is how you safely turn a timetable string into a UTC timestamp.

tour.title: Transit Service and Endpoints
tour.description: TransitServiceImpl ties the previous three steps together: it fetches through StptClient, caches each data kind in StaleCache with stale fallback, maps through TransitMapper and builds sorted, bbox-filtered, localized answers. TransitController exposes the public /transit endpoints (routes, stops, vehicles, arrivals, alerts, last departures and a home summary) with Accept-Language-based language selection, and TransitSummaryResponse and LastDeparturesResponse power the 'last tram at this hour' idea from Step 1.

tour.title: Testing Transit with Fixtures
tour.description: Each transit layer has its own tests. StptClientImplTest runs the client against a mocked HTTP server fed saved STPT responses such as arrivals-stop-1.json and vehicles-route-1.json, TransitServiceImplTest mocks the client and uses MutableClock to check caching, stale fallback and last departures, and TransitControllerTest verifies every endpoint and the SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE mapping. Recorded fixtures mean the tests never depend on live.stpt.ro being up.
tour.languageLesson: @WebMvcTest loads only the web slice of Spring, so controller tests run fast with the service replaced by a mock.

tour.title: Backend Build and Tooling
tour.description: build.gradle targets Java 21 and Spring Boot with JPA, Security and Validation, while the Gradle wrapper pins a fixed Gradle version so every teammate builds the same way. The application-local properties example lists the Supabase URL, JWT secret and pooler connection each developer fills into a git-ignored local profile.
tour.languageLesson: The Gradle wrapper (gradlew plus gradle-wrapper.properties) downloads the pinned Gradle version on first run, so nobody needs Gradle installed globally.

tour.title: The Expo Mobile App
tour.description: Switching to the client, _layout.jsx is the Expo Router root and index.jsx is the Discover screen rendering a react-native-maps MapView centered on Timișoara using the map.js helpers. api.js resolves the backend URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL so the app can call the endpoints built above, and package.json pins Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81, expo-router and react-native-maps.
tour.languageLesson: Expo Router uses file-based routing: _layout.jsx wraps every screen in its folder and index.jsx becomes the default route. Only EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables reach app code, inlined at build time, so never put secrets in them.
